zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 1/Main Deck level; they obstruct the view downward from Decks 4, 5, and 6, with Deck 4 experiencing the most obstruction and Deck 6 the least, while horizon views remain clear.
zones.effect: You lose the view straight down to the water but keep the ocean horizon; some guests find the boats themselves an eyesore in photos.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to first-time cruisers who envision unobstructed water views and photographers; experienced cruisers and those focused on horizon views typically don't mind.

zones.what: Deck 9 aft cabins sit directly below the Lido Deck pool area and buffet on Deck 10.
zones.effect: Expect noise from deck chairs scraping, foot traffic, and early-morning buffet setup starting around 6:00-6:30 AM.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and late risers should avoid; early risers and those out of the cabin most of the day won't notice.

zones.what: Deck 7 forward cabins sit two decks below the Lido Deck pool and buffet area.
zones.effect: Some noise transmission from pool deck activity, but dampened by the intervening deck; less severe than Deck 9 aft but still noticeable during peak hours.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers may notice during busy pool times; most guests find it tolerable given the distance.

zones.what: Deck 5 and 6 forward cabins sit above the Universe Lounge main showroom, which spans Decks 3-4 forward.
zones.effect: Show noise typically ends by 10:30-11:00 PM; bass and applause can transmit upward, especially on Deck 5.
zones.mattersTo: Early-to-bed guests and families with young children should consider midship or aft; night owls and show-goers won't mind.

zones.what: Deck 6 and 7 aft cabins sit above the main dining rooms on Decks 4 and 5 aft.
zones.effect: Galley service noise and dining room activity during meal times; kitchen prep can start as early as 5:30-6:00 AM.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those sensitive to early-morning noise should avoid; most guests find it acceptable given dining hours are predictable.

zones.what: Primary elevator banks are located midship, with stairwell access at forward, midship, and aft positions on each deck.
zones.effect: Cabins near midship elevators offer maximum convenience but experience hallway traffic and bell chimes; cabins farther forward or aft trade some walking for quiet.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests and those prioritizing convenience should stay near elevators; light sleepers and those seeking quiet should avoid immediate elevator adjacency.

zones.what: Engine room sits low and aft; Deck 4 and 5 aft cabins, particularly those farthest aft, experience low-frequency vibration when engines are running.
zones.effect: Subtle but constant vibration and hum, most noticeable at night in calm seas; some guests find it soothing, others find it prevents sleep.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive sleepers should avoid; those who sleep through white noise or find engine hum comforting may prefer these cabins for their lower price.

zones.what: Bow thrusters operate low and forward during maneuvering in port; Deck 4-6 forward cabins hear the thruster tunnel activity during arrival and departure.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical grinding noise for 10-20 minutes during docking and undocking, typically early morning arrival and evening departure.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers docking in port early morning will be awakened; heavy sleepers and those already awake for port days won't mind.

zones.what: Anchor chain runs through the bow; Deck 4-6 forward cabins, especially those closest to the centerline, hear anchor deployment and retrieval.
zones.effect: Loud metallic rumbling for 5-10 minutes during anchor operations, typically 6:00-7:00 AM on tender port mornings.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone sleeping during tender port arrivals will be awakened; useless to avoid if you're already up for port.

zones.what: Main crew corridor (I-95) runs along the centerline with access points near midship elevator areas on all cabin decks.
zones.effect: Cabins immediately adjacent to crew access doors experience periodic crew traffic, particularly during service hours (early morning, meal times, evening turndown).
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers near crew doors may notice hallway activity; most cabins are sufficiently distant that this is not a factor.
